title: Two of the three Queensland LNG ventures accepted a reservation scheme; only Santos opposed it
oneLiner: The industry's own split weakens the claim that reservation is unworkable.
body: Reporting around the May 2026 announcement described the LNG industry as broadly supportive, chiefly to end ad hoc interventions by successive governments, with Australia Pacific LNG and Shell's QCLNG accepting the policy and Santos's GLNG preferring the status quo. GLNG is also the venture that has drawn most on domestic gas to meet export contracts.
contextBackground: Which producers objected, and why, is a useful check on the investment-deterrence argument: the objector is the venture with the least domestic supply and the most to lose.
contextDisagreement: Agreed as fact. Producers say acceptance was pragmatic, not endorsement; critics say it shows the scheme asks little of two of the three.

evidenceItems.citation: ABC News, 7 May 2026 — industry broadly supportive; Illawarra Mercury (AAP), 'Gas export project to stop dipping into domestic market'

otherClaim.title: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix

claimItself.title: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix
claimItself.oneLiner: The producers' central objection: forced local sales at any price make new fields harder to finance.
claimItself.body: Australian Energy Producers argued the draft imposed complex and opaque compliance obligations, would undermine trust with Asian buyers, and would deter investment. Santos's chief executive said forcing sales at any price could 'kill companies'; a smaller producer called the scheme 'nationalisation by stealth'. If new supply does not come, the argument runs, prices rise regardless of reservation.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Two of the three Queensland LNG ventures accepted a reservation scheme; only Santos opposed it

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim contradicts “Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix”
